claims.title: the elementary near-parameter calculus.
claims.reasoning: The Near subgroup is the image-coefficient filtration, not the ideal generated by a unit. Multiplication, monotonicity, unit cancellation and the WIS23 coordinate criterion are exact.

claims.title: Frobenius improves the filtration and detects constants.
claims.reasoning: The actual Frobenius fixes the coefficient basis and raises zeroth Witt coefficients to the pth power. The constant criterion uses p-divisibility in each Z_p coordinate and the nonunit tau_s; p=2 and s=0 remain covered.

claims.title: a near-divisible component idempotent is zero.
claims.reasoning: Two uses of image saturation give e=d r_0+tau s. Idempotence gives arbitrary Near order, and then arbitrary p-divisibility; the argument needs no domain hypothesis on B_0.

claims.title: detection of every component's constant coefficient.
claims.reasoning: The corrected statement leaves tau independent of i_0(T), as the original const_dvd does. Total DVR divisibility, a nonzero component idempotent and IFD3 prove the full generic conclusion.

claims.title: the precise integral-series normal form.
claims.reasoning: The induction extracts only a tuple of constant coefficients, then cancels t^m. The infinite series is defined through finite sums in each coefficient and works for every original component index.

claims.title: full near-parameter closedness modulo the prime.
claims.reasoning: The bounded-pole presentation and IFD5 give the exact normal form at order m. Telescoping the successive approximants against one formal series proves near_closed without T-completeness of E_0.

claims.title: the actual image is fixed, has bounded poles, and is near-closed.
claims.reasoning: The actual character equality and injectivity force trivial resGamma on H. WSer.EE_dense at precision p supplies the pole presentation. WIS supplies precisely the injection, saturation and separation hypotheses of the original generic closed implication.

claims.title: sharp-root coordinates preserve the exact fixed group.
claims.reasoning: The representative estimate gains one p-adic order at every pth power, including p=2. actT_coeff and the actual isometric actC give sharp-root equivariance. LS1 applies to the same Hinf and original action; a zero coefficient gives the exact flat norm bound.

claims.title: integral coefficients in the finite cyclotomic layers.
claims.reasoning: The lifted residue-basis construction gives a DVR with uniformizer p; simple-root lifting supplies the prime-to-p roots in the same K_0. Distinct fractional valuations show that integral finite-layer expansions have integral coefficients, including p=2,r=1.

claims.title: every completed integral element has a generator lift.
claims.reasoning: The lift subring contains p O_C. The explicit compatible sequence u^(p^N a^k) has the prescribed Nth coefficient and belongs to the original IsTiltOf generator family. Density in the same cyclotomic completion gives every required residue lift.

claims.title: the full original invariant tilt approximation.
claims.reasoning: Exact sharp roots are Hinf-fixed before approximation. Matching the same Nth coefficient gives |x-w|flat <= |p|^(p^N); the valuation-ring divisibility criterion supplies the original epsilon-power approximation. No additive sharp map or cohomology premise is used.

claims.title: fractional invariant approximation with a common pole.
claims.reasoning: The integral threshold works for every larger N, with fixed s. The identity epsilon-1=tau_s^(p^s) gives the requested tau_s exponent. The proof permits every original s and every fixed fractional element.

claims.title: the correct fixed coordinates in a good layer.
claims.reasoning: The original Good field inclusion gives Hinf subset H. The actual tensor action fixes the O factor, so fixedness passes to the same finite Witt coordinates and their zeroth coefficients.

claims.title: elements eventually in the coefficient image form a subring.
claims.reasoning: Persistence under a ring endomorphism and a common maximum prove the eventual-image set is a subring. No perfectness or inverse Frobenius on the coefficient image is presumed.

claims.title: approximation inside any subring containing the generators.
claims.reasoning: The inverse-image/constant-coefficient construction lifts the generated subring without asserting additive Teichmuller lifting. A common pole exponent across the finite basis and the exact Near cancellation give the claimed arbitrary-subring approximation.

claims.title: the actual invariant approximation has eventual coefficient values.
claims.reasoning: The epsilon-root generators enter the eventual-image subring by the exact Witt Frobenius formula. Original IoW identifies each prime-to-p root tilt with the corresponding integral embedding tuple. The approximant is not incorrectly required to be fixed.

claims.title: one prime-adic step for the kernel.
claims.reasoning: Every original additive hypothesis is retained. The recurrence d_(m+1)=Phi d_m-delta advances the filtration; near closedness and saturation give the one-step kernel division.

claims.title: injectivity on the quotient by the coefficient subgroup.
claims.reasoning: The repeated one-step division gives z in D+p^kN for every k, and exactly the supplied p-adic closedness gives z in D. No group topology or torsion assumption is inserted.

claims.title: one prime-adic step for the cokernel.
claims.reasoning: The convergent filtration sum has the correct sign for Phi-1. Both telescoping identities and saturation of the residual term are checked; the zero approximant legitimately invokes near closedness.

claims.title: the full original additive quotient bijectivity theorem.
claims.reasoning: The p-weighted construction produces surjectivity under the original arbitrary-natural-p additive hypotheses. Additivity alone commutes Phi with the weights, and closedness supplies the final exact coefficient error.

claims.title: a finite coefficient matrix has one contracting filtration.
claims.reasoning: One finite maximum controls all matrix poles. The direct product calculation does not cancel a potentially nonunit t. The shifted filtration m+c_0+1 contracts because Frobenius doubles Near order.

claims.title: eventual smallness uses one common iterate.
claims.reasoning: One common iterate works for the finitely many coordinates. The iterated matrix is constructed using preimages of finitely many entries; neither injection of j_0 nor surjectivity of phi_0 is assumed.

claims.title: the full generic matrix quotient theorem.
claims.reasoning: The seven displayed groups of hypotheses match the original generic matrix theorem. Coordinatewise sums, saturation and closedness, with the exact shift, verify every hypothesis of IFD20; the matrix need not be invertible.

claims.title: the actual fixed-vector descent and its surjectivity companion.
claims.reasoning: The actual specialization keeps the original K,s,H, coefficient basis, maps and rings. WIS18/19/20/25 plus IFD2/7/16 supply every generic premise. The additional surjectivity conclusion follows from the same full generic theorem.

claims.title: full inhomogeneous invariant Frobenius-matrix descent.
claims.reasoning: The rectangular inhomogeneous equation is vectorized with coefficients (A_0)_(ik) C_(ell j), using A_1 C=1. The Y C term is preserved. Both original invertibility assumptions and zero-rank cases are retained at the endpoint.

claims.title: exactly one period-ring supplier remains before Wach existence.
claims.reasoning: The WLD26 join uses WIS18 and IFD25 with Y=0 on the same actual maps and fixed group. Actual prism existence, original tied/IsStd period data and crystalline realization remain premises; no unconditional WachEx, HW/Fon/Cmp or global denominator closure is claimed.

scope: All 26 human arguments and exact original generic/actual endpoint scopes, including the full inhomogeneous Rational.main. The sharp-root argument is a proved simplification using LS1/LS4. Formal correctness is accepted; no Lean replay.

resolved_findings.finding: The initial statement imposed i_0(T)=tau although original Rational.const_dvd quantifies tau independently. Its written proof did not use that condition.
resolved_findings.resolution: Author removed the unused equality from IFD4. IFD5 and actual applications keep their separate definition t=c(i_0(T)). The full original independent-tau scope is now proved.

limitations: Actual Wach prism, tied/IsStd period data and crystalline realization remain premises of the conditional IFD26 return. Separate FaithH, EtBasis, Herr/quantitative comparison and the common global ConclF family remain outstanding.
